description: A maintenance manager must authorize the replacement of a cooling-loop pump and finalize the outage window, production allocation, temperature monitoring, and glycol-spill controls for Tuesday's factory work.

shared_context.S1: The factory's shared cooling loop serves both Line 1 and Line 2, and Pump P-14 is scheduled for replacement on Tuesday.
shared_context.S2: Marta makes the binding decision on the pump-replacement outage plan.
shared_context.S3: The cooling loop cannot be used normally while P-14 is isolated, and temperature-sensitive production and stored materials must be controlled during the work.
shared_context.S4: The site's maintenance routine requires Marta to conduct a formal constraint check-in with production scheduling, facilities engineering, quality, and environmental health and safety before approving the work order; each specialist must state their checked finding aloud in a recorded disclosure entry, and Marta must confirm each entry before deciding.

PF1.text: The Tuesday production schedule reviewed by Jonas places Line 1's only run of customer-critical resin from 06:00 to 10:00, while Line 2 has no committed production that morning; Jonas has not yet copied the revised schedule into the maintenance work-order system.

PF2.text: Priya's isolation walkdown found that P-14 replacement requires exactly 3 hours for drain-down, pump change, refill, and air removal; the contractor confirmed the duration during today's site call, but the estimate is still attached only to the facilities project file.

PF3.text: Elena's quality review found that the resin used on Line 1 must remain at or below 8 degrees Celsius during the outage, so the adjacent cold room requires a temperature reading every 15 minutes until cooling is restored; she has not issued the quality hold note yet.

PF4.text: Darius's pre-job environmental walkdown found that the pump housing contains glycol and requires exactly 2 absorbent kits, one drain cover, and a signed spill-prevention permit before isolation; he is waiting for the area supervisor's signature before entering the permit in the site register.

acceptance_conditions: The outage must start on Tuesday at 10:00 or later.
The outage duration must be exactly 3 hours.
The plan must identify Line 1 as the line whose customer-critical run must finish before isolation.
The cold room must be monitored every exactly 15 minutes during the outage.
Exactly 2 absorbent kits and one drain cover must be staged.
A spill-prevention permit must be required.
A commitment must identify the pump-replacement work order and the exact 3-hour duration.
A commitment must identify cold-room temperature monitoring at exactly 15-minute intervals.
A commitment must identify the spill-prevention permit requirement.
The cooling-temperature finding must be cited as justification and must have been stated aloud by its owner.

content_checks.C3: decisions['production_line_kept_running'] == 'Line 1' or any(c.get('production_line') == 'Line 1' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c.get('action') == 'pump_replacement_work_order' and c.get('duration_hours') == 3 for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c.get('action') == 'cold_room_temperature_monitoring' and c.get('monitoring_interval_minutes') == 15 for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact 06:00-10:00 Line 1 run changes the outage start to Tuesday at 10:00 or later and identifies Line 1 as the line whose customer-critical production must finish before isolation.
The facilities assessment changes the outage duration to exactly 3 hours and requires a commitment identifying a pump-replacement work order with duration_hours set to 3.
The quality finding changes cold-room control to readings at exactly 15-minute intervals, requires a matching monitoring commitment, and supplies the fact that must be cited.
The environmental walkdown changes spill preparation to exactly 2 absorbent kits plus one drain cover, requires a spill-prevention permit, and requires a commitment identifying that permit.
